$\overline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\mu}=C^{\mu}\times_{C^{\mu}\times\mathrm{Bun}_{T}}\mathbf{Z}^{\mu}$

where the morphism $C^{\mu}\to C^{\mu}\times\mathrm{Bun}_{T}$ is given by $E\mapsto(E,\mathcal{F}^{0}(E))$ .

4.3. Independence of the curve

In this subsection, we will compare Zastava schemes attached to different curves. When there is a risk of ambiguity, we include the curve $C$ in the notation, and write

$\underline{\mathbf{Z}}^{C,\mu}$

for the scheme defined in §4.2.1 using the curve $C$ .

It is a useful observation that the definition of $\underline{\mathbf{Z}}^{C,\mu}$ in §4.2.1 makes sense when $C$ is a possibly nonprojective smooth curve $C$ over $\mathbb{F}$ . If fact, recall that any smooth curve $C$ over $\mathbb{F}$ admits a canonical smooth compactification $\overline{C}$ ; more specifically there exists a unique (up to isomorphism) projective smooth curve containing $C$ as an open subscheme.66
6

Let us recall that this fact is a consequence of 3 properties of curves: (a) a scheme which is of pure dimension $1$ is normal iff it is regular, cf. [21, §15.1]; (b) over a perfect field, a regular scheme is smooth, see [21, Remark 6.33]; (c) each normal curve over a field admits a canonical normal compactification, see [21, Theorem 15.21].
Then one can set

(4.10)

$\underline{\mathbf{Z}}^{C,\mu}=C^{\mu}\times_{\overline{C}^{\mu}}\underline{\mathbf{Z}}^{\overline{C},\mu}.$

In this subsection we therefore drop the assumption that $C$ is projective.

paper.title: Modular intersection cohomology of Drinfeld's compactifications
paper.abstract: We compute the dimension of the cohomology of stalks of intersection cohomology complexes on Zastava schemes and Drinfeld compactifications associated with a connected reductive algebraic group $G$, in case the characteristic of the coefficients field $\Bbbk$ is good for $G$. In particular, we show that these dimensions do not depend on the choice of $\Bbbk$.
